label: Tables, Keys & Capacity Model
desc: 15 interview questions covering Fundamentals, Keys, Capacity, Performance.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: DynamoDB is a fully managed, serverless NoSQL database service provided by AWS that handles large-scale, high-performance distributed workloads.

subs.label: Keys
subs.desc: The partition key (hash key) determines which physical partition stores an item, based on a hash of the key's value.

subs.label: Capacity
subs.desc: Throughput measures a table's read/write capacity — how many read and write operations per second the table can handle, expressed in read and write capacity units.

subs.label: Performance
subs.desc: How do you handle hot partitions in DynamoDB?

label: Indexes, Queries & Advanced Features
desc: 15 interview questions covering Indexes, Consistency, Querying, Transactions and more.

subs.label: Indexes
subs.desc: Secondary indexes let you query on non-key attributes, providing flexible access patterns beyond what the table's primary key alone supports — DynamoDB offers two kinds: Local Secondary Indexes and Global Secondary Indexes.

subs.label: Consistency
subs.desc: What is eventual consistency in DynamoDB? What is strong consistency in DynamoDB?

subs.label: Querying
subs.desc: Use the Query API to retrieve items matching a specific partition key value, with optional sort key conditions to narrow the range — this is the efficient, key-driven way to read from DynamoDB.

subs.label: Transactions
subs.desc: How do you handle transactions in DynamoDB?

subs.label: Batch Operations
subs.desc: What is batch processing in DynamoDB?

subs.label: TTL
subs.desc: TTL (Time To Live) automatically deletes items after a specified expiration timestamp attribute is reached, useful for managing data expiration (session data, temporary caches) without writing cleanup jobs.

subs.label: Data Modeling
subs.desc: How do you design DynamoDB tables?
